_comment: Allowlist for ci/disclosure-scan.mjs. This file is the INVERSE of a denylist:
it may only ever contain strings that are already safe to publish in a public
repository. Never add a personal name, login, or personal address here — the
scan patterns are derived at run time and are never committed.
Adding an entry is the intended, review-visible way to clear a false positive.
_creditPaths: The product's own credit surface. The About screen names the people who built the app and links to their sites, on purpose, as user-facing content — so a derived identity there is intended publication, not a leak. Only paths are listed; no name is named. Structural rules still apply here.
_platformIdentityEmailDomains: Author identities on these domains are the forge/CI itself, not people. Dropping [bot] names alone is not enough: the Actions identity has a human-shaped name that occurs legitimately in workflows and docs.
_nonIdentifyingMailDomains: Consumer mail providers. An author address on one of these still yields name/address/local-part patterns, but the domain itself identifies nobody, so no domain pattern is derived from it.
_emailDomains: Domains an added line may carry: documentation placeholders, our own product, the forge, and the fixture domains already used by the server and mobile test suites.
_emailLocalParts: Role addresses. Matching on the local part rather than the domain lets the automated commit trailers pass without this file naming the services that send them.
_fileExtensionTlds: Asset filenames such as logo@2x.png are email-shaped. Treat these trailing labels as file extensions, not domains.
_githubLogins: Only bare profile URLs are flagged (github.com/<login> with no repository segment), so organisations we link to by repository need no entry. These are the reserved GitHub paths and our own org, which are bare by nature.
_applicationIdLabels: Our own product label. A derived identity match is excused only inside a reverse-DNS application identifier carrying one of these — see isExemptApplicationId. The label being excused is never named here.
_homeUsers: Shared, non-identifying account names. A home directory named after a person is the finding this rule exists for.
